text: The negative Coombs test and normal hematocrit effectively rule out hemolytic disease of the newborn. Given the isolated indirect hyperbilirubinemia in a thriving, exclusively breastfed infant with no signs of infection or liver dysfunction, the clinical picture is classic for breast milk jaundice. DIAGNOSIS READY: Breast milk jaundice
